reviews.title: Great concept but…
reviews.text:
I have the 30 oz Tumbler the 2.0 version. The bottle really helps me hit my water intake, I have POTS and have to drink 120oz a day, which is difficult without support. 

However, the syncs are constantly wrong!! I follow the instructions to the T, I recalibrate the sensor after each time I charge the battery, I always wait for the light to recognize that it has weighed the new weight when I refill. I always refill after completely empty and make sure that the sensor has time to recognize the empty bottle. 

However, without refilling a 30z bottle it will sync 60-80 oz. Over and over again. 

Huge amounts like 13.6 oz or 20.3 oz at a time!

So. It’s a great concept but currently the sensors and the app sync just don’t work in real life. 

Disappointing for such an expensive water bottle.

reviews.title: App doesn’t sync
reviews.text:
I bought the new PRO 2 model on Wednesday. It worked for the first few hours, but since Thursday, every single drink log has been stuck in a perpetual spinning loop. The app clearly reads the exact ounces from the bottle via Bluetooth, but the data never actually finalizes, leaving my daily progress total sitting at 0 ounces day after day.

I have tried every single troubleshooting method available: force-closing the app, toggling Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, completely disabling the Apple Find My integration, performing a hardware soft reset on the puck sensor using a pin, and ensuring all software versions are fully updated. Absolutely nothing works to push the backlog through.

The only remaining workaround is to delete the stuck logs and manually enter my water intake, which completely defeats the purpose of paying a premium for an automated smart bottle. The hardware is nice, but the app is completely broken. Save your money until they release a functional firmware patch.

reviews.title: I absolutely love this bottle!
reviews.text:
I’ve never been a water drinker, or a bottle fan. I certainly don’t own a Stanley. I bought a lined/timed bottle and it sat untouched all day. Knowing dehydration was probably the cause of my headaches and brain fog, I bought the Pro 2. 

I’m easily drinking 100oz a day now. The lights blinking and the beep and the watch notification are a perfect reminders to take a sip. The cup and app work flawlessly. I genuinely feel better. 

I would love to see a pin or favorite option on beverages. Even a way to reorder them would be helpful. I have to scroll past 5 alcohol options to get electrolytes.

reviews.text: I also use the Larq app with a Larq bottle. I like the Hydrate bottle better but I use both. The Larq data syncs correctly. The Hydrate app doesn’t. Sometimes it syncs and reports correctly. Unfortunately most of the time it sits clocking sync with Health then reports whatever is in the Health database as negative water intake or it never completes and shows zero intake even though it shows the intake records. It’s comical really that they can’t even get the basic required functionality working reliably but at the dance time they have the gall to charge a subscription fee to add drinks other than water. That’s absolutely idiotic. Do better.
